free_tier.stated: Free deposit, no published cap. 'Is there a cost to deposit data in BioStudies? No, both deposition of data to BioStudies and data access are free of charge.' Docs discuss 'larger data volumes (hundreds of GiB)' as routine.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: Binding constraint on read is per-ip-shaping. 1 stream 7 KB/s, 16 parallel 25 KB/s against the EBI FTP edge. Retention: permanent, DOI auto-assigned; files can sit 'hold until published' indefinitely before release.

egress.terms: Free and anonymous. 'Anonymous downloads are enabled' over FTP; also HTTPS. No egress meter anywhere in the docs.

tooling: Submission Tool + FTP + Aspera (ascp) in; anonymous FTP/HTTPS out. Path is predictable: /biostudies/<mode>/<COLL>/<COLL0-99>/<ACC>/Files/ where mode is `fire` or `nfs`.
chaining: ArrayExpress is a BioStudies collection, so one account covers both. Unlimited accessions per account; each accession gets its own directory tree. Read side anonymous per-file HTTP, so it fronts to a CDN trivially.
limits_note: Per-object-cap: none stated; Aspera recommended above 10 GiB. Binding constraint on read is per-ip-shaping. 1 stream 7 KB/s, 16 parallel 25 KB/s against the EBI FTP edge. Retention: permanent, DOI auto-assigned; files can sit 'hold until published' indefinitely before release.

identity_cost.detail: depositing needs a BioStudies submission-tool account, created with a name, an email address and a password; the ORCID field is optional. No card and no phone number is asked for. Reading published data needs no account at all.

reliability_note: Read edge is slow per connection and stalls connections under parallel load (one of 16 timed out with 0 bytes). Fetches from the same EBI edge as ENA/PRIDE, so they are one throughput pool, not three.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.
